slot.brief: Radioactive sample with given half-life decays for a stated multiple of the half-life; find the fraction of the sample remaining (or nuclei disintegrated).

stem: A radioactive sample has a half-life of $6$ h. What fraction of its original nuclei remains after $24$ h?

verdicts.working: 24 h is 4 half-lives, so the remaining fraction is (1/2)^4 = 1/16.

working:
$n=\dfrac{24}{6}=4$ half-lives. $\dfrac{N}{N_0}=\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^4=\dfrac{1}{16}$.

Independent check: 24 h is 4 half-lives, so the remaining fraction is (1/2)^4 = 1/16.
solution:
The number of half-lives elapsed is $n=\dfrac{24}{6}=4$. Hence,
$$\dfrac{N}{N_0}=\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^4=\dfrac{1}{16}.$$
